note.text: Eduction here means deriving a categorical claim from a single categorical premise by transforming terms or quality. Simple conversion exchanges the complete subject and predicate. It preserves truth for E and I under the stated standard meanings. A does not convert simply: all voters may hold badges without every badge holder voting. With an explicit existing subject, A supports conversion by limitation to some P are S. O does not generally convert. Distinguish a truth-preserving equivalence from a weaker consequence requiring existence.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to transform a categorical claim by a licensed operation and reject an unsupported converse. Builds on: opposition, complete terms and counterexample models. Leads to: obversion and chains of immediate inference.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: No club voters are unregistered persons converts to No unregistered persons are club voters. Some volunteers are readers converts to Some readers are volunteers. All voters are badge holders does not give All badge holders are voters. If at least one voter exists, it does give Some badge holders are voters.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Mark complete S and P, exchange them and keep the original quantity and quality for simple conversion. Check whether the original form permits it. For a limited A consequence, state the existence premise and avoid claiming full equivalence.

cards.idea: Read the whole example before identifying its function.
example: No S are P becomes No P are S.
Some S are P is equivalent to Some P are S.
All voters have badges does not imply all badge holders vote.
All S are P plus existing S implies Some P are S.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve scope, terms and assumptions.
example: Conversion means changing only the predicate to non-P. Correction: That describes part of obversion, not switching terms.
Every categorical form converts simply. Correction: A and O have counterexamples.
All S are P always means All P are S. Correction: P can contain additional members outside S.
The universal alone proves an existing witness in the stated convention. Correction: An existence premise is needed.
